heading: Rejection is mechanical, not capability-gated
text:
### Rejection follows the content, not the setting [LNRE.4.2]

A regex-less runtime decides whether it can load a DSC from the
artefact's `requires` ([RDSC.16.2.8]), which the compiler computes from
what the artefact contains, not from its settings. A DSC whose content
uses regex lists `regex` there, and a build without an RE2-class engine
refuses it with `DS_ERR_DSC_CAPABILITY_ABSENT` before decoding any body
([RDSC.16.2.7]). The runtime trusts `requires` and does not check it
against the content ([RDSC.16.2.8]).

This is what makes the capability's absence safe rather than merely
conventional. A DSC that happens to contain no regex loads on a
regex-less runtime whatever its `regex` setting; a DSC that does contain
one is refused whatever its setting. `regex: false` changes only when
the author learns about a mismatch — at compile time instead of at load
time ([LNRE.1.3], [LNRE.2.3]) — never whether the runtime accepts the
artefact.
